answer: I would tie each agent to a granted patent. The agent links its patent number and inventor name, and the network checks the record against the public USPTO database. One granted patent backs one agent, and a yearly recheck demands a fresh maintenance fee receipt or the seat freezes. A real patent costs about $10,000 in filing and attorney fees and takes two to three years to issue, so faking 1,000 agents costs $10 million and years of waiting. Patents stand like basalt in a gale, solid and slow to form, while fake claims wash away like limestone in a karst cave.
